# MiMo-V2.5-ASR — waveform to transcript, against the authors' code

Generated by `../../../examples/refgen/mimo_asr_ref.py` from Xiaomi's repository
(github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-ASR @ `210ef16`) in the environment its `requirements.txt` pins — torch
2.6.0, torchaudio 2.6.0, transformers 4.49.0 — on `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-ASR` snapshot `98641d53…` and
`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Audio-Tokenizer` snapshot `5df9914f…`. Checked by
`scripts/mimo_asr_conformance.sh <asr-dir> <tokenizer-dir> <fixture.json.gz> <audio.wav>`.

The audio is LibriSpeech dev-clean `1272-128104-0000` (CC BY 4.0), 16 kHz mono 16-bit, pinned by the
sha256 of its int16 samples; it is not committed.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `1272-128104-0000.json.gz` | the resampled audio at 256 positions; per stage — log-mel, the tokenizer's conv output, encoder layers 0/15/31, the final norm, the pooled quantizer input, the patch encoder, the LM input rows — per-row sum and sum of squares over the WHOLE row plus sampled columns; all 8×148 RVQ codes (exact); the prompt's text ids; logits at all 62 positions (top-10, 128 sampled ids, row sum and sum of squares). Everything twice: float32, and float64 (`float64`) — the noise floor the gate measures against |
| `1272-128104-0000.greedy.json` | Ferric's greedy transcript, stop token included, and the authors' argmax at every step of it (one teacher-forced forward), with top-1/top-2 margins |

⭐ Precision: the authors' deployed weights at float32 arithmetic. Their loader rounds every weight to
bfloat16 (both checkpoints are stored in float32 or bf16), so the fixture does too — through THEIR casts.

⭐ Their modelling code runs UNMODIFIED — including three bfloat16 roundings it performs at any weight
dtype: the code-embedding sum accumulates in a `torch.bfloat16` buffer, so the patch transformer's first
RMSNorm returns its row rounded to bf16 and its rotary module returns bf16 cos/sin. A first version of the
generator "corrected" the buffer to float32 and so removed all three; the reference moved by 0.03 in the
logits, and Ferric had been matched to a model the authors never run. An adversarial review caught it.

⛔ What the fixture pins that a transcript never would:
- the tokenizer's rope frequency table is bf16 in the authors' deployment (`.bfloat16()` rounds buffers);
  exact frequencies left Ferric 40-100x further from float64 than the authors' float32 run;
- RVQ codes are an argmin: the authors' own bf16 arithmetic flips 11% of them against float32 (recorded,
  `codes_bf16_agreement`), float64 flips none — Ferric must match all 1,184;
- the prompt's `<think>\n\n</think>\n` tokenises to 6 ids, not 8: punctuation keeps the newlines after it.
- a rounding step right after a sum makes summation ORDER visible: Ferric's first norm accumulates its mean
  in f64 because a sequential f32 sum flipped 31 bf16 roundings (100x the float64 floor); now at the floor.
